# LoRa offline PHY fixtures

## Independent source and reproducibility

`vectors.json` and the little-endian complex-float32 (`.cf32`) waveforms were
actually generated by the unmodified **gr-lora_sdr** encoder/modulator, not by
PWN's decoder or a reciprocal PWN encoder:

- https://github.com/tapparelj/gr-lora_sdr
- Revision `862746dd1cf635c9c8a4bfbaa2c3a0ec3a5306c9`
- GNU Radio 3.10.12.0, native C++ gr-lora_sdr built with CMake and installed
  in an isolated `/tmp/pwn-lora-install` prefix during development.
- SF7/CR4, SF7/CR1, SF8/CR3, SF8/CR2; explicit header, CRC enabled,
  bandwidth = sample rate = 125000 Hz, eight preamble upchirps, sync 0x12,
  128 trailing zero samples. CR1 means 4/5, CR4 means 4/8.
- Input text and encoded symbol output are recorded literally in `vectors.json`;
  its SHA256 values pin every waveform. Tests verify the hashes.
- `generate.txt` records the exact fixture-generation script. It uses the
  external GNU Radio Python bindings only as a fixture-generation interface,
  never as a PWN runtime dependency or automatic test requirement.

Build the pinned upstream revision outside this repository:

```sh
cmake -S /tmp/pwn-lora-sdr-ref -B /tmp/pwn-lora-build \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/tmp/pwn-lora-install -DENABLE_DOXYGEN=OFF \
  -DPYTHON_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/python3
cmake --build /tmp/pwn-lora-build -j4
cmake --install /tmp/pwn-lora-build
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/pwn-lora-install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
  /usr/bin/python3 spec/fixtures/sdr/lora/generate.txt
```

The upstream transmitter is GPL-3.0 licensed and is **not** copied, linked into,
or distributed with PWN. These fixtures are its signal/data output, using
first-party literal test messages. The receiver coding equations instead adapt
MIT-licensed LoRaPHY:
https://github.com/jkadbear/LoRaPHY/blob/4fddd9a7b47682781c663608bfc4f196e4bf656d/LoRaPHY.m
(Gray mapping, diagonal interleaving, Hamming parity, whitening, five-bit header
checksum and payload CRC). Full copyright and permission notice are retained in
`documentation/LoRaPHY-LICENSE.txt`.

Paper: Zhenqiang Xu, Pengjin Xie, Shuai Tong, Jiliang Wang, *From Demodulation to
Decoding: Towards Complete LoRa PHY Understanding and Implementation*, ACM TOSN
2022, https://doi.org/10.1145/3546869 .

## Supported receive mode and evidence boundary

The Ruby receiver supports **SF7-12, CR4/5 through CR4/8, explicit or configured
implicit headers, optional payload CRC, LDRO, and normal/inverted IQ**. Bandwidth
is 125/250/500 kHz; finite input sample rates >= bandwidth are resampled by a
streaming windowed-sinc filter with a rational clock and bounded phase table.
The existing VOLK dot-product kernel accelerates this filter when available;
Ruby provides the fallback. Native/Ruby sample parity is tested to 1e-6.

Implicit mode requires `implicit_header: true`, `payload_length: 0..255`, and
matching `cr: 1..4`, `crc: true/false`. Explicit mode obtains length, CR and CRC
presence from the checked header; its header is authoritative, not the `crc`
option. `ldro: nil` automatically enables LDRO for symbol periods >16ms; true
and false explicitly override this. `invert_iq: true` conjugates the input.
The first eight symbols always use SF-2 and CR4/8, including implicit mode;
subsequent LDRO blocks use SF-2 rather than SF rows.

Output is raw `payload_hex`, not LoRaWAN plaintext or a validated LoRaWAN MIC.
Header checksum and FEC are checked (single-bit correction for 4/7 and 4/8;
detection only for 4/5 and 4/6). A present payload CRC must pass. Absent checks
are **not** reported as valid: `crc_valid: nil` for CRC-disabled packets and
`header_valid: nil` for implicit packets, alongside explicit presence/mode flags.

Tests exercise both upstream waveforms and separately synthesized IQ from the
recorded upstream symbols, arbitrary chunk boundaries (including single scalar
I/Q components), timing offsets, integer-bin CFO, repeated identical packets,
FEC corruption, header corruption, payload CRC corruption, silence, noise,
truncation, missing SFD, unsupported options, and an open-pipe callback before
EOF. The public runner uses quantized cs16 input; Base does not currently accept
cf32 sources directly. Loading fixtures with `unpack('e*')` is for the direct
floating-point demodulator API only.

## Expanded independent mode vectors

`generate_modes.txt` uses the same pinned, unmodified upstream transmitter.
`modes.json` records 14 additional payloads, mode settings, upstream encoded
symbols and SHA256 hashes of gzip-compressed float32 IQ. No fixture encoder
calls receiver routines. The cases cover:

- SF9/CR1 explicit CRC; SF10/CR2 explicit without CRC.
- SF11/CR3 and SF12/CR4 explicit with CRC and LDRO.
- SF9/CR2 implicit with CRC; SF12/CR1 implicit, LDRO, inverted, without CRC.
- SF7/CR4 explicit inverted with CRC and implicit without CRC.
- SF8/CR3 implicit with CRC; SF10/CR4 implicit with LDRO and without CRC.
- SF11/CR1 and SF12/CR2 explicit with LDRO forced off (CRC on/off respectively).
- SF8/CR2 explicit CRC at 500000 input samples/s and 125000 Hz bandwidth.
- SF9/CR3 explicit CRC at 300000 input samples/s and 125000 Hz bandwidth.

The noninteger-rate case starts with upstream 500000-sample/s modulation, then
uses SciPy `resample_poly(3, 5)`, independently of the receiver resampler. Inverted
vectors conjugate upstream IQ. These transformations are specified in the
reproducible generator; they are not separate captured-radio observations.
All new waveforms pass the public cs16 `.decode` path. Same-rate variants are
also tested in scalar, 8192-scalar and whole-waveform chunks; the noninteger-rate
case uses scalar, 194-scalar and whole-waveform chunks. Every variant rejects
75%-length truncation. Original corruption and open-pipe tests remain passing.
This is named-mode coverage, not every possible mode/length/channel combination.

## Benchmark and remaining limits

`benchmark.txt` runs actual chunked IQ-to-payload decoding (8192 float scalars
per call); `benchmark-results.json` records a host run with existing native FFT
and VOLK support. Ratios are signal duration / decoding wall time: 1.962–4.301
for the new same-rate vectors, 1.502 at 300000 input samples/s, and **0.839 at
500000 input samples/s**. Thus the latter is still slower than real time on this
host. The pure-Ruby resampler was slower still (0.175 and 0.277 for the 500000
and 300000 vectors before native acceleration). Fixture loading, source unpack,
logging, live input and hardware are outside these timings.

These are deterministic generated PHY interoperability vectors, **not captured
RF**. Measured RF sensitivity, multipath resilience, collisions, fractional-bin
CFO tracking, sample-clock drift compensation and guaranteed real-time reception
remain unverified or unimplemented. Only integer-bin CFO is verified. Input
rates below bandwidth are rejected; arbitrary ratios are implemented but only
1x, 2.4x and 4x input/BW are independently exercised here. Resampling needs
lookahead (roughly 16 output samples); captures must include the packet tail,
not end at its last nominal symbol sample. `.detect` retains the older,
separately labelled preamble-only detector. No automatic RF source is opened
by these tests.
